Social Media Syndicate [6254]

By: Jana Marx | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look at how a criminal enterprise is running a drug syndicate via apps like EskomSePush, Uber and Telegram - and employing children as drug mules.

Unique Selling Point:
We get to film a sting operation along with Crime Intelligence and get exclusive interviews with some of these "runners" (child drug mules).

Summary:
Apps we use every day, like EskomSePush and Uber, social media platforms like TikTok and Facebook Marketplace, and messaging apps such as Telegram (basically any app with a “people near me” or “groups near me” function) are being utilized to run a drug syndicate. And children are getting drawn into it.

Further information:
Trafficking, drugs and the distribution of illicit goods have always been around. As technology evolves, it’s becoming easier and easier – and much more difficult for parents to safeguard their children.

Now some criminals in South Africa have stooped to a new low: Apps we use every day, like EskomSePush and Uber, social media platforms like TikTok and Facebook Marketplace, and messaging apps such as Telegram (basically any app with a “people near me” or “groups near me” function) are being utilized to conduct illegal business. And children are getting drawn into it.

“Business” involves prostitution, drugs (from weed to heroin and prescribed meds), guns and the forging of official documents.

The groups where “business” is conducted have names like “BMW fans”, “Grand Central Apartments”, “Midrand buy and sell” – so group names that don’t raise suspicion at all.

A child innocently stumbling upon these things, will be pushed more similar content – that’s just how these apps’ algorithms work.

The investigation is now run by Crime Intelligence, along with a criminal informant. They managed to establish it’s run by a single syndicate, with mid-level “bosses” based in especially Jhb, Cape Town and Durban.

These guys potentially have ties with companies outside South Africa – I have seen the size and clarity of the crystal meth they sell and it’s not the stuff you sommer get locally.

The adults running this syndicate is “employing” children to do the dirty work for them. The children targeted are as young as 12/13 years. They prey on the children’s curiosity and also on their socio-economic circumstances. If you are an underaged addict and you need money to pay your drugs, or you are starving at home and need money to survive, you can become a “runner” (dealer, seller, courier) to pay your “debt”. Runners use, amongst others, apps like Uber o to courier drugs to clients. If there are no drugs to sell, you can pay your debt with sex (also a service that’s being rendered).

The SAPS is planning a bust to arrest some of these runners to get to the main guys.

We're going to add our own undercover element by either filming the informant doing an actual transaction, or doing it ourselves. The "how" TBC.

Press Release:


Sting in the Tale

Technology is turning the tide in the fight against the illicit drugs trade and its many associated crimes. For better and worse. These days, anyone wanting to get their hands on hard drugs
needn’t risk the danger and uncertainty of the black market. With the evolution of social media and online apps, criminals are having a field day marketing their illicit goods to people from all spheres of society and – scarily - to any child with access to
a phone. From pornography to street and prescription drugs, to guns and forged official documents, all are for sale on many of the platforms we rely on every day: community information apps, e-hailing, social media and messenger apps with a “people near me”
function. Carte Blanche follows a Crime Intelligence-driven investigation into online drug running as we join a sting operation and listen to harrowing stories of victims having to pay with their bodies when they fail to reach the sales targets set by their
criminal bosses.

Producer: Jana Marx | Presenter: Derek Watts

Watch the trailer


Script:


1 BUST INTRO “Police! Get down! Get down! Get down! On the ground! Get down! Down!”


ACT 1

2 VO It’s Centurion, Pretoria, mid-November. Police are cracking down on a crime syndicate that’s been sprouting right under our noses - in our homes..using social media platforms and cell phone apps to lure innocent victims into its trap.

3 INTRO LINK
This story starts about two years ago.. just before the Covid pandemic hits..when a businessman - a concerned citizen - opens the loadshedding app EskomSePush and notices it’s not all about loadshedding…

4 VO
Our concerned businessman discovers that the app EskomSePush, meant to help communities connect around shared interests and informatioN…is being used as a trading room for illicit goods.

5 VO
On similar apps with community chat forums, the businessman even spotted sellers boasting about the quality of their weed offerings. And saw obscure menus of prescription and illicit street narcotics with names like snow, lollipops…shrooms…

6 VO
It soon became clear that, where most of us would use these apps as the developers had intended… there was a world of criminal operators who’d hijacked platforms for their sinister agenda.

7 PHONE CALL: DRUG DEAL

“Hello?”
“Is that Problem Child?”
“Yes, how can I help you?”

8 VO
Clicking on the ASK MY STREET function on EskomSePush, our businessman ordered whatever he could… dagga that shouldn’t be sold like this …and CAT, a synthetic street drug.

9 VO
Dealers are quick to take the conversations off the app and onto private texts. We set up a hidden camera to see if the businessman’s deal would pay off.

10 UPSOUND - audio recording
“....I saw your message on the Eskom App…Have you got CAT?”

“I can make it for R200 per gram.”

“Bring me five…”

“You sure you are coming? I don’t want to wait around for nothing, nè?!”

“No, I’m coming.”

11 VO
The goods arrived by motorcycle.

12 UPSOUND
“I just bought this from a dealer…”
(up until Derek asking: For that whole packet hey?)
“Yes, for a whole packet a R1000.”

13 VO
An undercover policeman confiscated the drugs and logged the deal as part of the ongoing investigation…

14 (VISUALS)

15 VO
In his online trawling, our businessman had encountered a young woman we’ll call “Charity” who’d grown up in Joburg’s Alexandra township.

16 Charity UPSOUND: 0;32 My mom passed away when I was still young. My father, I didn't know anything about him. I was raised by my aunt.

17 VO
With minimal parental input in her life, Charity was desperate for friends. One day she nicked her aunt's phone to create a Facebook profile. She chatted on the old messenger app MXit.

18 Charity UPSOUND: 4;03 I started inviting friends. And there was this other girl at school. She was big…She was in grade 11. And then she started like being friends with me on on MXit. Every time when I go to school, she'll be like, Come, Come sit with us.

19 VO
Her new friend soon invited her to a party - the affirmation she was yearning for. Once there, something felt off... For one thing, some guys were older and spoke in strange accents.

20 (VISUALS)

21 Charity UPSOUND: 5;35 They wanted to give me alcohol. I said no. And then they insisted 5;52 I got drunk. We were dancing and dancing.

22 VO
Another girl called Charity into a bathroom.

23 Charity UPSOUND: 6;32 She took out a small pack, a bag. I didn't know what it was. 7;07 The next thing when I wake up, I'm in a strange room with this guy, I don't know really what happened but something happened.

24 VO
The man had raped her and threatened her not to tell anyone - the drugs did their quick and devastating work … Soon her new dealer friend helped her get more…

25 Charity UPSOUND: 9;26 And then she introduced me to those guys again - Nigerian guys. And then they told me if I can bring small girls like me to them, I'll get more bags for free.

26 VO
Charity became a runner with a sales target to reach. If she ran into debt, they’d make her pay it off in other ways.

27 Charity UPSOUND: 13;26 I’ll sleep with them, their friends…people come and say I want you to sleep with that guy…

28 VO
In Sunnyside Pretoria we met another young woman we’ll call Faith.

29 VO
Now 18, she was also befriended on Facebook and invited to a party.

30 Faith UPSOUND: 5;16 I felt dizzy that time, then I slept. Then when I woke up I found my panty with blood. I was feeling pain. I was raped.


31 Faith UPSOUND: 5;37 You were just 13? Yes, I was only 13. They took away my virginity that time.

32 Faith UPSOUND: How did you feel? I felt guilty because I didn't tell my mom the truth. I told her that I'm going to sleep at my friend's. I didn't tell her that I'm going to a party. 6;10 I kept on using drugs because I was trying to put the guilt away.

33 REFLECTIVE LINK:
“No matter how many stories I’ve done, many involving children, I just don’t think I’ve been as upset as interviewing those two girls…


ACT 2

34 VO
Our concerned businessman felt much the same way…WHEN his world collided with Charity and Faith’s online - they’d been dealing for five years already.

35 VO
Hoping to help them, he turned police informant and helped kick-start a top secret investigation into the criminals using social media and apps as their sales platform.

36 VO
The operation stretches across country boundaries and private business.

37 SAPS UPSOUND: 2;31 We've seen some really horrific scenes, which is heart rendering. We have come across some children as young as you said, 12 years old, younger than that…

38 VO
Captain Dave Miller is the police spokesperson.

39 SAPS UPSOUND: 4;33 From our investigation, we've been able to establish that round about 10 to 15 odd years they've been building up their the networks and with the boom of social media, every second child has got a tablet has got a cell phone has access to the internet…

40 VO
The team found they weren’t dealing with the odd individual looking to make a quick buck…but an organised network that could provide their informant illicit goods …from firearms to drugs to pornography…grooming children to do the drug trafficking and be trafficked.

41 Christiaan UPSOUND: 11;11 Remember, this type of crime is high profit, low risk, and it's very anonymous.

42 VO
Psycho-criminologist Professor Christiaan Bezuidenhout.

43 Christiaan UPSOUND: 11;56 I think the big thing that happened with drug dealing now online, is that the risk towards the seller has reduced and the risk towards the buyer has increased. 11;56 Now, the seller can be picky. He can follow people for a long time on social media.

44 VO
Investigators followed the anonymous online cat and mouse games between faceless personalities…and saw that the online deals needed real-world wheels.

45 UBER LINK: E-hailing services are a lifeline for carless city commuters. But these apps in the wrong hands are enabling drugs to be delivered at your doorstep…

46 SAPS UPSOUND: 5;20 So they love using Uber and Bolt. That's the way they get to you. Nobody's gonna suspect that Uber.

47 VO
For years, nobody suspected Charity or Faith as they couriered drugs around.

48 Christiaan UPSOUND: 14;07 And now they use these children, because they're not responsible. The police are not allowed, according to the law, to apprehend and to process the child up to prosecution under the age of 12 years. So it's a non-risk for this person to use the child as a runner. 37;13 It was brutal - they were invited to a so-called party. They were plastered with alcohol and drugs and they were raped? 37;24 That's also a typical process of what some of the human traffickers do. It’s brutal - then they’ve got her…


Act 3

49 LEGAL LINK: Fake profiles, jumping between social media platforms and using emoji’s to fool moderators… It seems like criminals are having a field day in cyberspace, with little to no consequences...

50 VO
Pretoria University Professor Sizwe Snail KAMTUZE has just written the definitive textbook on South Africa’s Cyberlaw.

51 Sizwe UPSOUND: 03:48 With social media comes the phenomenon of anonymity. But trust me, you are still leaving a forensic trial, if they do want to track it down, they most probably can.

52 VO
And this team really wanted to… slowly but surely the evidence mounted… Then it was D-Day – a sting operation to remove selected runners to further the broader investigation.

53 BUST UPSOUND “Police! Get out! Get out!”
“Sorry, sorry, Sir. I’m not armed. Sorry.”

54 VO
Runners who’d unwittingly been talking to a police informant for months faced the moment of truth.

55 BUST UPSOUND “You are under arrest for the possession of drugs…”

56 VO
A search of the car yields a bag of mandrax. Investigators take personal and work cell phones together with drug evidence.

57 Police station background noise

58 VO
But runners are clearly only a start - the big question is what will APP creators do? Social media lawyer Diana Schwarz is also a child rights activist.

59 DIANA UPSOUND: In cases, like faith and charity being recruited on a social media platform or app, could the owners directors developers of that app be prosecuted?

Diana:
They can be if they had knowledge of the circumstances that were occurring on the site and they did nothing about it.

Derek:
So if they are made aware of this app being used for drug running, and they don't remove the content, they are guilty of a crime?

Diana:
Yes, certainly they are.

60 VO
None of the companies whose platforms are being used, would speak to us on camera. But in a statement, Uber said they were concerned, because children under 18 have to be accompanied by an adult on rides. Uber met with the police after our request for an interview.

61 VO
Bolt said they workED hard to keep their platform safe and acknowledged IT WAS difficult for a driver to identify a minor without asking for an ID. They said they’D cooperate with the police.

62 VO
As for EskomSePush where the deals had started, its developers said they weren't aware of the activity on their platform, but were always taking steps to improve the app's automatic detection mechanismS .. and encourage users to report illicit or explicit content.

63 VO
But will it pay off? For our businessman, who helped Faith and Charity escape the syndicate, there’s no time to waste.

…This is an ongoing war.

64 BUST UPSOUND: He’s arrived…

Get down on the ground now!!!!!

And then they told me if I can bring small girls like me to them, I'll get more bags for free. 26 VO Charity became a runner with a sales target to reach. If she ran into debt, they’d make her pay it off in other ways. 27 Charity UPSOUND: 13;26 I’ll sleep with them, their friends…people come and say I want you to sleep with that guy… 28 VO In Sunnyside Pretoria we met another young woman we’ll call Faith. 29 VO Now 18, she was also befriended on Facebook and invited to a party. 30 Faith UPSOUND: 5;16 I felt dizzy that time, then I slept. Then when I woke up I found my panty with blood. I was feeling pain. I was raped. 31 Faith UPSOUND: 5;37 You were just 13? Yes, I was only 13. They took away my virginity that time. 32 Faith UPSOUND: How did you feel? I felt guilty because I didn't tell my mom the truth. I told her that I'm going to sleep at my friend's. I didn't tell her that I'm going to a party. 6;10 I kept on using drugs because I was trying to put the guilt away. 33 REFLECTIVE LINK: “No matter how many stories I’ve done, many involving children, I just don’t think I’ve been as upset as interviewing those two girls… ACT 2 34 VO Our concerned businessman felt much the same way…WHEN his world collided with Charity and Faith’s online - they’d been dealing for five years already. 35 VO Hoping to help them, he turned police informant and helped kick-start a top secret investigation into the criminals using social media and apps as their sales platform. 36 VO The operation stretches across country boundaries and private business. 37 SAPS UPSOUND: 2;31 We've seen some really horrific scenes, which is heart rendering. We have come across some children as young as you said, 12 years old, younger than that… 38 VO Captain Dave Miller is the police spokesperson. 39 SAPS UPSOUND: 4;33 From our investigation, we've been able to establish that round about 10 to 15 odd years they've been building up their the networks and with the boom of social media, every second child has got a tablet has got a cell phone has access to the internet… 40 VO The team found they weren’t dealing with the odd individual looking to make a quick buck…but an organised network that could provide their informant illicit goods …from firearms to drugs to pornography…grooming children to do the drug trafficking and be trafficked. 41 Christiaan UPSOUND: 11;11 Remember, this type of crime is high profit, low risk, and it's very anonymous. 42 VO Psycho-criminologist Professor Christiaan Bezuidenhout. 43 Christiaan UPSOUND: 11;56 I think the big thing that happened with drug dealing now online, is that the risk towards the seller has reduced and the risk towards the buyer has increased. 11;56 Now, the seller can be picky. He can follow people for a long time on social media. 44 VO Investigators followed the anonymous online cat and mouse games between faceless personalities…and saw that the online deals needed real-world wheels. 45 UBER LINK: E-hailing services are a lifeline for carless city commuters. But these apps in the wrong hands are enabling drugs to be delivered at your doorstep… 46 SAPS UPSOUND: 5;20 So they love using Uber and Bolt. That's the way they get to you. Nobody's gonna suspect that Uber. 47 VO For years, nobody suspected Charity or Faith as they couriered drugs around. 48 Christiaan UPSOUND: 14;07 And now they use these children, because they're not responsible. The police are not allowed, according to the law, to apprehend and to process the child up to prosecution under the age of 12 years. So it's a non-risk for this person to use the child as a runner. 37;13 It was brutal - they were invited to a so-called party. They were plastered with alcohol and drugs and they were raped? 37;24 That's also a typical process of what some of the human traffickers do. It’s brutal - then they’ve got her… Act 3 49 LEGAL LINK: Fake profiles, jumping between social media platforms and using emoji’s to fool moderators… It seems like criminals are having a field day in cyberspace, with little to no consequences... 50 VO Pretoria University Professor Sizwe Snail KAMTUZE has just written the definitive textbook on South Africa’s Cyberlaw. 51 Sizwe UPSOUND: 03:48 With social media comes the phenomenon of anonymity. But trust me, you are still leaving a forensic trial, if they do want to track it down, they most probably can. 52 VO And this team really wanted to… slowly but surely the evidence mounted… Then it was D-Day – a sting operation to remove selected runners to further the broader investigation. 53 BUST UPSOUND “Police! Get out! Get out!” “Sorry, sorry, Sir. I’m not armed. Sorry.” 54 VO Runners who’d unwittingly been talking to a police informant for months faced the moment of truth. 55 BUST UPSOUND “You are under arrest for the possession of drugs…” 56 VO A search of the car yields a bag of mandrax. Investigators take personal and work cell phones together with drug evidence. 57 Police station background noise 58 VO But runners are clearly only a start - the big question is what will APP creators do? Social media lawyer Diana Schwarz is also a child rights activist. 59 DIANA UPSOUND: In cases, like faith and charity being recruited on a social media platform or app, could the owners directors developers of that app be prosecuted? Diana: They can be if they had knowledge of the circumstances that were occurring on the site and they did nothing about it. Derek: So if they are made aware of this app being used for drug running, and they don't remove the content, they are guilty of a crime? Diana: Yes, certainly they are. 60 VO None of the companies whose platforms are being used, would speak to us on camera. But in a statement, Uber said they were concerned, because children under 18 have to be accompanied by an adult on rides. Uber met with the police after our request for an interview. 61 VO Bolt said they workED hard to keep their platform safe and acknowledged IT WAS difficult for a driver to identify a minor without asking for an ID. They said they’D cooperate with the police. 62 VO As for EskomSePush where the deals had started, its developers said they weren't aware of the activity on their platform, but were always taking steps to improve the app's automatic detection mechanismS .. and encourage users to report illicit or explicit content. 63 VO But will it pay off? For our businessman, who helped Faith and Charity escape the syndicate, there’s no time to waste. …This is an ongoing war. 64 BUST UPSOUND: He’s arrived… Get down on the ground now!!!!!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We look at how a criminal enterprise is running a drug syndicate via apps like EskomSePush, Uber and Telegram - and employing children as drug mules.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We get to film a sting operation along with Crime Intelligence and get exclusive interviews with some of these "runners" (child drug mules).
metadata.Summary: Apps we use every day, like EskomSePush and Uber, social media platforms like TikTok and Facebook Marketplace, and messaging apps such as Telegram (basically any app with a “people near me” or “groups near me” function) are being utilized to run a drug syndicate. And children are getting drawn into it.
metadata.Further information: Trafficking, drugs and the distribution of illicit goods have always been around. As technology evolves, it’s becoming easier and easier – and much more difficult for parents to safeguard their children. Now some criminals in South Africa have stooped to a new low: Apps we use every day, like EskomSePush and Uber, social media platforms like TikTok and Facebook Marketplace, and messaging apps such as Telegram (basically any app with a “people near me” or “groups near me” function) are being utilized to conduct illegal business. And children are getting drawn into it. “Business” involves prostitution, drugs (from weed to heroin and prescribed meds), guns and the forging of official documents. The groups where “business” is conducted have names like “BMW fans”, “Grand Central Apartments”, “Midrand buy and sell” – so group names that don’t raise suspicion at all. A child innocently stumbling upon these things, will be pushed more similar content – that’s just how these apps’ algorithms work. The investigation is now run by Crime Intelligence, along with a criminal informant. They managed to establish it’s run by a single syndicate, with mid-level “bosses” based in especially Jhb, Cape Town and Durban. These guys potentially have ties with companies outside South Africa – I have seen the size and clarity of the crystal meth they sell and it’s not the stuff you sommer get locally. The adults running this syndicate is “employing” children to do the dirty work for them. The children targeted are as young as 12/13 years. They prey on the children’s curiosity and also on their socio-economic circumstances. If you are an underaged addict and you need money to pay your drugs, or you are starving at home and need money to survive, you can become a “runner” (dealer, seller, courier) to pay your “debt”. Runners use, amongst others, apps like Uber o to courier drugs to clients. If there are no drugs to sell, you can pay your debt with sex (also a service that’s being rendered). The SAPS is planning a bust to arrest some of these runners to get to the main guys. We're going to add our own undercover element by either filming the informant doing an actual transaction, or doing it ourselves. The "how" TBC.
